title: Human resources for health information system: minimum data set for health workforce registry (2015) — system functional requirements
description: System types and functional requirements from the WHO guide 'Human resources for health information system: minimum data set for health workforce registry' (2015, ISBN 9789241549226), held in this library as 9789241549226-eng. Owner, 2026-11-01: an inspirational, non-definitional reference for the DTH-HRH handbook's Chapter 7 (Functional Requirements); these concepts contribute to a definition and are not definitional, so no term carries skos:definition. Three kinds of concept: system types (Figure 3: the health information system, its sub-systems, the HRH information system and its functional components, among them the health workforce registry); the four functional domains (Figure 4, Table 1) and Table 2's information categories; and one concept per functional-requirement block of library/9789241549226-eng, broader-linked to the system type it is stated for and related to its domain or category. Labels are the source's own words; a requirement the source gives no name is labelled with its full statement. The minimum data set itself (Table 3, the data-element sheets, Tables 6-7) is deliberately not represented. Every term is a candidate until a person confirms it.

terms.prefLabel: In a national context an electronic health workforce registry can be considered the single authoritative source of health workforce information that can provide an accurate count of all health care personnel that either have worked or are currently working at national or sub-national levels, including in the private sector.
terms.scopeNote: An inspirational, non-definitional functional requirement (system-requirement-statement), word for word from pages 16-18.

terms.prefLabel: An electronic health workforce registry can be designed to authenticate and validate the existence of a health worker and provide essential details about that person.
terms.scopeNote: An inspirational, non-definitional functional requirement (system-requirement-statement), word for word from pages 16-18.

terms.prefLabel: In addition, a health workforce registry can ensure quality control, provide easy access to information on production, distribution and utilization of health personnel, and assist in budgeting, research development and advocacy.
terms.scopeNote: An inspirational, non-definitional functional requirement (system-requirement-statement), word for word from pages 16-18.

terms.prefLabel: A health workforce registry allows aggregation of health workforce data in several combinations and assists both national and sub-national ministries of health in producing essential indicator-based reports, as needed.
terms.scopeNote: An inspirational, non-definitional functional requirement (system-requirement-statement), word for word from pages 16-18.

terms.prefLabel: The health workforce registry is a central and essential component of a functional HRIS, as it contains important health worker attributes that can subsequently be linked to other relevant HRIS components.
